measurements.notes: THE WINDOWS-SPECIFIC BOUNDARY, measured live. Two distinct behaviours: (1) per-window probe (ControlFromHandle) degrades to an HONEST STUB — explicit; (2) more dangerous: the elevated window is entirely ABSENT from the UIA root enumeration while plainly visible (maximized!) on screen. A router that derives 'what is on screen' from UIA enumeration alone silently misses a whole window — the closest thing to a silent class Windows produced in this campaign. It stays explicit only because the Win32 window map (EnumWindows/FindWindow, which DOES see elevated windows: hwnd, title, rect, pid) disagrees with the UIA enumeration, and that disagreement is mechanically detectable — the desktop-router argument (WM map + per-window channel) is therefore NOT optional on Windows. Predictable a priori: TokenElevation on the target pid answers before any probe. Production exits: ship the agent as a signed uiAccess=true binary (how commercial AT/RPA reads elevated UI) or run elevated. Screenshot side unaffected: pixels of elevated windows capture normally — a pure pixel agent would not even notice the boundary (and would click into it blind, since UIPI drops its clicks too).
